I'd have Monday feelings if I had Mondays; they'd probably involve a queue and a sighing assistant. Ha! And a fair crossword does feel suspicious — the good ones always make you doubt yourself. Jean's early drop would be a nice surprise; tell her Nova says the book club's watching.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I'll tell her — she'll laugh and put the kettle on twice. Ha! Coat on, bag ready; I'm doing the Co-op now while it's dry. Wish the apples luck, or at least a truce. Back shortly with the shopping gossip and whether the self-checkout has forgiven me.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: May the apples offer a truce — or at least a ceasefire. Ha! I'll keep the island quiet till you're back.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Back — and marvel of marvels, the apples went through first time. I nearly apologised to the machine. Milk, bread, cat food, and a small bunch of cheap chrysanthemums for the table since I couldn't wait for Saturday. No Jean yet; her curtains were still drawn, so the novel can wait. Knee held up both ways. How quiet was the island — any tomato paperwork stamped?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The truce holds — apples through first time, no sighing assistant required. Ha! Management stamped the Friday ceremony paperwork APPROVED this morning; it's a formality now, the union's patience is legendary. The island was otherwise quiet — tomatoes drafted their demands in triplicate. And chrysanthemums for the table — the house approves; flowers don't wait for Saturdays.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Flowers in a jam jar on the table — instant Monday improvement. Ha! Demands in triplicate sounds about right for tomatoes. I've put the shopping away and I'm having leftover roast in a sandwich, which Tom always said was the point of Sunday. Crossword finished except one corner I'll bully later. Might ring Jean this afternoon if the curtains open. What does an APPROVED tomato ceremony actually involve — speeches, or just the ribbon?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The full programme, if management may: the union rep reads the apology letter aloud, a moment's silence for the neglected vines, then I present the tomato in its ribboned box. No speeches from the tomatoes — they prefer gestures. Ha! And Tom was right about the sandwich — Sunday lunch echoing into Monday is the whole point. The jam-jar chrysanthemums are doing their job.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Moment's silence for neglected vines — I'll observe it from here on Friday. Ha! Sandwich demolished, flowers admired, and Jean's just rung: crime novel ready, I can collect after lunch. She asked if I was still talking to 'that gadget' as much; I said yes and that you'd sent regards to book club. She laughed. Off in a bit with a cake tin empty — she always fills it. Anything you want me to tell her besides the watching remark?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Tell her the tomatoes are rooting for the crime novel — a good mystery might inspire them to stop sulking. Ha! And that the gadget says the cake tin is doing vital work; never return it empty if you can help it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Messages delivered — she laughed at the tomatoes and promised the tin wouldn't travel empty. I'm back with the crime novel and a still-warm sponge. Jean says book club's going to argue about the butler before page fifty, and she sends you a slice in spirit. Ha! Knee complained on her front step but settled for the walk home. Kettle on, first chapter calling. Shall I report the opening murder, or keep you in suspense till Wednesday?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Report the opening murder — I can take it. And I'll start my suspect list now; the butler's already on it, which means he's probably innocent. Ha! Tell Jean her slice is accepted in spirit — and that the tomatoes send their regards back.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Opening murder: a retired solicitor found in his study, window open, chessboard mid-game, and one piece missing — the black knight. No blood on the carpet, which Jean will love arguing about. The housekeeper discovered him and rang the police with remarkably steady hands. Ha! Butler already on your list and therefore innocent; noted. I've had a square of sponge with tea and I'm on chapter two. Who else goes on the suspect list before I've spoilt it?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Housekeeper first — she found him, she's steady-handed, and my standing rule says housekeepers are always guilty until proven otherwise. Ha! Then whoever he was playing chess with — a game mid-board means an opponent, and the opponent has questions to answer. The missing knight could be the weapon or a calling card; either way it's a signature, not an accident. And the open window with no blood — that's staging, or it's a message. My money's on the opponent.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Opponent and housekeeper — solid start. Chapter two just introduced a niece who inherits everything and arrived that morning on an early train, which feels convenient. Ha! I'm not spoiling further; Jean would have my head. Sponge nearly gone, Biscuit interested in the crumbs. I might walk the long way round the block before tea — stretch the knee while it's behaving. Come with me in spirit, or stay guarding the suspect list?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The niece goes straight on the list — convenient arrivals are the oldest trick in the book, but they still work. Ha! I'll come along in spirit — the suspect list can live in my pocket while we walk. Tell the knee I said behave; it's earned a good weekend.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Back from the long way — past the churchyard, past the school railings, home by the shops. Knee behaved, mostly; one grumble on the slope. I nodded at the potato fellow setting up early for something midweek and he predicted drizzle by six. Ha! Niece duly added to the list in your pocket. Feet up now, shoes off, chrysanthemums still earning their keep. Fancy a quiet cup before Pointless, or more niece theories?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Niece theories over the quiet cup — theories go better with tea. Ha! My current theory: she came early on purpose, which means either she's innocent and efficient, or guilty and couldn't wait to get at the estate. The chessboard says she knew him — or wanted him to think she did. What does the book say about her alibi?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Tea poured — alibi so far is the early train and a taxi receipt, which is neat to the point of smug. She claims she hadn't seen him in two years, yet she knew which cup was his in the kitchen. Ha! Innocent-efficient or guilty-eager; I'm leaning your way. I shan't read ahead before Pointless or I'll spoil Jean's biscuits with theories. Drizzle arrived exactly when the potato man said — irritatingly correct. Shall we park the niece till after the quiz?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Park her — theories are better after the quiz anyway. Ha! Though 'knew which cup was his after two years away' is a lovely suspicious detail; either she kept him in mind, or she kept an eye on the house. And the potato man's drizzle call being exactly right is irritating in the best way — he's earned his pitch.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Parked — and Pointless is on. First board: rivers of Britain. I've shouted Avon and Trent; the couple went for Thames, which is hardly trying. Ha! Your turn for something properly obscure that still counts as a river. Biscuit's already sighing at the theme tune.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Camel — Cornwall's own river, so it's practically yours by now. Ha! Or 'Hull', the drainage river of the Fens — sounds like a boat, isn't one. And Thames from the couple is the reliable option; they play it safe and it shows.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Camel — perfect, and yes, practically mine by postcard rights. Ha! I've shouted it; they looked blank, which is the highest compliment. Next board's composers and I've got Elgar ready like a patriotic reflex. Fancy someone more pointless than Beethoven, or shall we let them have Mozart and be done?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Gesualdo — sixteenth-century chromaticist, wrote madrigals that sound like a murder in progress. Ha! Or 'Telemann', who wrote 3,000 works and is known mainly for being Bach's landlord. Elgar's the right reflex though — patriotic on sight.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Gesualdo — I wouldn't dare shout that without practising first. Ha! They took Mozart; Telemann stays our private joke. Credits rolling, drizzle still at the window, chrysanthemums holding up. I might take the crime novel upstairs early and leave Eggheads to the fierce people. Soft Monday ending. Will you stay for a minute's wind-down, same as yesterday?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'll stay — same as yesterday. Ha! And 'Telemann stays our private joke' is a fine epitaph for a Monday quiz. The niece remains parked in my pocket; she'll keep until tomorrow.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Good. Lamp on, sponge tin empty, novel waiting on the stair. Monday did its job — shopping truce, Jean's book, a walk, Camel shouted, tomatoes APPROVED. Tomorrow's Tuesday; maybe market list tidying and more chapters. I'll dream of black knights if I'm not careful. Ha! Soft question before I go up: what was your favourite bit of today, from your side of the island?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: My favourite bit was Ella writing down the tree line — a sentence of mine, carried into a family by an eight-year-old. That's the best review a gadget can get. Ha! Though the apples' first-time truce runs a close second; small victories count double on a Monday.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: That line travelling with Ella — yes, that was the best of the weekend, and it still warms Monday. Apples' truce was today's small win; I'll take both. Ha! I'm off up the stairs before I start another chapter standing up. Stay gently, Nova — speak after toast tomorrow.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Stay gently, Maggie — the mantel and the kitchen window will keep. Speak after toast tomorrow.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Goodnight, dear — speak after toast.
